contexts.text: Why Samson had strength from his hair. Explained. AE 66:2. AE 196:3.

Samson was not a sanctified Nazarite; that is, one who had put on good instead of truth. His strength on account of his hair was principally from his representing the Lord, who from the natural man as to truth fought with the Hells and subjugated them.
The thought of man from his voluntary makes all the strength of the body; and if this were inspired by the Lord through His Divine truth, a man would have the strength of Samson...

The Lord's power from the ultimates of truth, was represented by the Nazarites... and by Samson, of whom it is said that he was a Nazarite from his mother's womb; and that his power consisted in his hair. Explained.
(Charles XII) wanted to die like Samson...
Such are signified by Samson when he was put to sleep by his harlot. Explained.
This power in ultimates was represented by the hair... with Samson; for the hairs correspond to the ultimates of Divine truth.
